§5.3 Block Classes

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-block-classes · rule layout blocks

✅ Normative

Every element MUST have exactly one of the seventeen classes below. Its layout class MUST match the class of the corresponding Markdown element defined in Elements§3.1. A class MUST NOT be chosen merely to complete a page: where the class is genuinely unclear, the output MUST NOT assert a class the page does not support.

The seventeen classes

Class Used for
Text One coherent paragraph or prose block
Title The overall document title, on its title or front page
Section-header A separate heading introducing a section or subsection
List-item One marked or hanging list item, including its continuation lines
Caption Text outside normal flow that names or explains a table, picture or formula
Footnote A footnote, source note, method note, or small explanatory note tied to the body
Page-header Repeated or page-specific content in the top margin
Page-footer Bottom-margin content — a page number alone qualifies
Picture A unified photo, diagram, chart, logo, map or molecular structure
Table A ruled or borderless row-and-column structure whose alignment matters
Formula A standalone displayed expression, including its displayed equation number
Checkbox-Selected A selected checkbox mark only — not its label
Checkbox-Unselected An unselected checkbox mark only — not its label
Code Preformatted source, commands, logs, or fixed-width output
Document Index A table of contents, index, or directory-like navigation block
Form Irregular controls or fields arranged for data entry
Key-Value Region A compact label/value group without a regular table grid

How each class is rendered in Markdown is set out in Elements§3.1.

One class across layout and Markdown

The layout box and the corresponding Markdown represent the same element and MUST use the same class. A producer MUST resolve a disagreement using the printed content and update both representations to agree. A detected label is only a suggestion — see Layout Regions§5.7.

The class describes the element's role; Markdown syntax alone does not determine it. Text and Footnote both render as paragraphs while keeping their distinct classes. A table or chart Caption uses <caption> inside its object's table HTML and keeps its own Caption class and layout box. A Picture rendered as <table data-source="chart"> keeps the Picture class; a printed Table has the Table class. The renderings prescribed in Elements§3.1 govern these cases.

The distinctions that decide most cases
Table vs Form A Table has a regular row-column structure. A Form has irregular fields or controls for data entry.
Table vs Key-Value Region A Table repeats rows and columns. A Key-Value Region is a compact label/value group with no regular grid.
Title vs Section-header Title is only the document's overall title on its cover — which sheet that is, is decided once in Document Type§4.4. A repeated title on a later page is Text or page furniture.
Caption vs Text Proximity is not enough. A Caption names or explains an object and sits outside normal flow. Ordinary nearby prose is Text.
Caption vs Footnote A Caption identifies an object. A Footnote adds a source, method, qualification or note.
Picture vs Formula A complex chemical structure is a Picture. An ordinary standalone mathematical expression is a Formula.
Checkbox The box covers only the square, circle or check mark — never its label.

The diagrams below are synthetic pages shown with their element overlays, one colour per class. There is no diagram yet for Checkbox-Selected, Checkbox-Unselected, Code, Document Index, Form or Key-Value Region; the definitions above govern those.

Title and Text

Title MUST be used only for the document's overall title. Authors, dates, addresses and other front-matter prose MUST stay separate Text elements.

✅ Sample — block-title-text

Red = Title · yellow = Text. A cover sheet. Expected boxes: one Title around the title and its Release 4.2.1 line, then three Text elements — the authors, the foundation's address, the date. Each Text element keeps its printed line break.

Section-header and List-item

Each visually distinct Section-header MUST be its own element. Each list item MUST be one List-item element, including its bullet or number and every continuation line.

Example B: three numbered items, each one List-item whose box takes in its number and its wrapped second line.

Footnote and Formula

Each distinct Footnote MUST be its own element. A Formula MUST contain the complete displayed expression and its equation number; inline maths stays part of its Text element.

✅ Sample — block-footnote-formula

Dark green = Footnote · grey = Formula · yellow = Text. Example A: two columns of body text and the footnote a) under the left column. Example B: a clipped neighbouring column, a paragraph with inline maths, and footnote 1. Example C: prose interrupted by the numbered displays (1) and (2), each one Formula with its number; the prose above, between and below them is four Text elements. The clipped fragments at the right edge of Example C (Figu, layer, …) have no box in the overlay and are left out.

Page-header and Page-footer

Page-header and Page-footer cover marginal content outside the main flow. Widely separated components of one band MUST be separate elements, and a page number alone qualifies as a Page-footer.

✅ Sample — block-header-footer

Bright green = Page-header · teal = Page-footer · red = Section-header · yellow = Text. Four excerpts. A: two Page-headers (file name left, draft stamp right) over Text, a Section-header and Text. B: two Page-headers (running section title, folio 9) over two paragraphs. C: a paragraph over two Page-footers (folio 4, running title). D: a paragraph over three Page-footers — a centred For internal use only, then the copyright line and the running title. A small solid black bar after the copyright line carries no text and has no box.

## Picture, Caption and Table

A Picture MUST include the complete unified graphic but **exclude its Caption**. A Table MUST
include the complete row-column structure but exclude its Caption and surrounding prose. See
[Block Boundaries](05-layout-block-boundaries.html)<span class="sec">§5.2</span>.
